constitution.title: नेपालको संविधान (Constitution of Nepal, 2072/2015), Unicode text as amended to Bhadra 2081
constitution.note: Linked from lawcommission.gov.np (Constitution category). Arts. 56 (three tiers: federation, provinces, and local levels; provinces made of the districts in Schedule 4; rural municipalities, municipalities, and district assemblies at the local level), 62 (President elected by an electoral college of the members of the Federal Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies, with weighted votes, by majority with a runoff), 84 (House of Representatives: 165 members by first-past-the-post from 165 constituencies and 110 by closed-list proportional representation with the whole country as one constituency), 85 (five-year term unless dissolved), 86 (National Assembly: 56 members elected, eight from each province including at least three women, one Dalit, and one person with disability or from a minority, by an electoral college of the Provincial Assembly members and the chairs and vice-chairs of rural municipalities and mayors and deputy mayors of municipalities with weighted votes, plus three nominated; six-year terms with one third retiring every two years), 176 (Provincial Assemblies: twice the province's House constituencies by first-past-the-post, as 60 percent, and 40 percent by proportional representation), 177 (five-year term), 215 and 216 (chair and vice-chair, mayor and deputy mayor by first-past-the-post; four or five women and two or three Dalit or minority executive members elected by the assembly within 15 days), 220 (district assembly of the local chiefs and deputies elects the District Coordination Committee: a chief, a deputy chief, and up to nine members), 222 and 223 (each ward elects a ward chair and four members by first-past-the-post, at least two of them women), 225 (five-year term of the village and municipal assemblies), and 275 (a referendum on a matter of national importance when two thirds of all members of the Federal Parliament so decide).

ecn_constitutional.title: Constitutional Provision (Part 24, Arts. 245-247 of the Constitution of Nepal)
ecn_constitutional.note: Art. 246(1): the Election Commission conducts, supervises, directs, and controls the elections of the President, the Vice-President, the Federal Parliament, the Provincial Assemblies, and the local bodies, and prepares the voters' list; Art. 246(2): it holds referendums on subjects of national importance.

Ballots are counted per constituency after the boxes of its polling centres are brought to the counting site, and the Commission publishes candidate votes by constituency only (result books and result.election.gov.np); no polling-centre or local-level breakdown is published.
classes.note: 165 single-member constituencies by plurality (Art. 84(1)(a)), elected together with the 110 proportional seats on two ballots. Five-year term unless dissolved (Art. 85). The 1991-1999 and 1959 Houses under earlier constitutions are separate classes.
classes.locator: https://giwmscdnone.gov.np/media/pdf_upload/%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%95%E0%A5%8B%20%E0%A4%B8_%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A8%20unicode%20%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%20%E0%A5%A8%E0%A5%A6%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%A7_mtbuyjt.pdf (Art. 84(1)(a): one hundred sixty-five members elected by the first-past-the-post system, one from each of 165 constituencies)

cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant constituency seat is filled at a by-election (House of Representatives Member Election Act 2074).

classes.name_en: National Assembly elections: 56 members chosen by provincial electoral colleges
classes.note: Electoral college of each province: its Provincial Assembly members and the chairs and vice-chairs of rural municipalities and mayors and deputy mayors of municipalities, with weighted votes (Art. 86(2)(a)); about 2,050 voters in all. cadence.runoff_rule: Runoff between the top two if no candidate wins a majority of the college's total weighted vote; a further vote if neither passes 50 percent (Art. 62(4)-(5)).

classes.name: प्रदेश सभा सदस्य निर्वाचन (पहिलो हुने निर्वाचित हुने)
classes.name_en: Provincial Assembly elections: the 330 first-past-the-post seats
classes.finest_note: The Provincial Assembly constituency, two in each House constituency; published by constituency only.
classes.note: Each of the seven Provincial Assemblies elects twice as many first-past-the-post members as its province has House constituencies, 60 percent of its seats (Art. 176(1)(a)); polled with the House. Five-year term unless dissolved (Art. 177). The 2026 House election did not include the Provincial Assemblies, whose next general election is due by late 2027.

access.evidence: The 2074 and 2079 Provincial Assembly result books (2079: one national book of 596 pages and one per province).

dates.note: First phase: 74 constituencies in 32 districts.
Second phase: 256 constituencies in 45 districts.

classes.name: प्रदेश सभा सदस्य निर्वाचन (समानुपातिक)
classes.name_en: Provincial Assembly elections: the 220 proportional seats (one list vote per province)
classes.note: 40 percent of each Assembly by closed-list proportional representation with the province as one constituency (Art. 176(1)(b)); seven list contests per general election.

access.evidence: The Provincial Assembly result books give each party's list vote by province and constituency.

dates.note: The list contests cover both 2074 phases.

classes.name: मुख्यमन्त्री
classes.name_en: Chief Minister of a province
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the province head as the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Provincial Assembly (Art. 168); not an election.

classes.name: प्रदेश प्रमुख
classes.name_en: Province head (governor)
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the President for five years (Arts. 163 and 165).

classes.name: जिल्ला समन्वय समिति निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: District Coordination Committee: chief, deputy chief, and members, elected by the district assembly
classes.note: Each district assembly, of the chairs and vice-chairs and mayors and deputy mayors of its local levels, elects a chief, a deputy chief, and up to nine members including at least three women and one Dalit or minority member (Art. 220(3)), within 30 days of the local results; the Commission runs it under its District Coordination Committee Election Directive.
classes.disposition_reason: Results are declared by each district's election officer and were not found in any central publication of the Commission.

classes.name: गाउँ तथा नगर कार्यपालिका सदस्य निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: Women and Dalit or minority members of the rural and municipal executives, elected by the assembly
classes.note: Within 15 days of the local results the village or municipal assembly elects four (five) women and two (three) Dalit or minority members to the executive (Arts. 215(4) and 216(4)).
classes.disposition_reason: Declared locally by the election officer of each local level; no central publication of these results was found.

classes.name_en: Local level by-elections
classes.note: Vacant chief, deputy, ward chair, and ward member posts, filled at by-elections called by the Commission (Local Level Election Act 2073).

classes.name: स्थानीय निकाय निर्वाचन (गाउँ विकास समिति, नगरपालिका)
classes.name_en: Village development committee and municipality elections, 1992-2006
classes.note: Chairs, vice-chairs, and ward members of about 4,000 village development committees and the mayors and ward members of the municipalities, elected directly in 1992 and 1997; the elected bodies lapsed in 2002, and the 2006 municipal elections under royal rule were boycotted by the main parties. The district development committees elected by them are a separate indirect class.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of these results was found on the Commission's site, which carries nothing before 2017.

classes.name: जिल्ला विकास समिति निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: District development committees (1992-2002), elected by the village and municipal members
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by electoral colleges of the village and municipal office holders, with no official count published.

classes.name: गाउँ र नगर पञ्चायत निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: Village and town panchayat elections (1962-1990), and the Kathmandu municipal election of 1953
classes.note: Partyless elections of village and town panchayats, whose members in turn chose the district and zonal panchayats; the first election in Nepal was that of the Kathmandu municipality in 1953.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of these results is known online.

classes.name: न्यायाधीश
classes.name_en: Judges
classes.disposition_reason: Judges of the Supreme Court, High Courts, and District Courts are appointed on the recommendation of the Judicial Council (Arts. 129, 140, 149, and 153); none are elected.

classes.name: गैर-क्षेत्रीय निर्वाचन
classes.name_en: Non-territorial and out-of-country representation
classes.disposition_reason: No seats are elected by a non-territorial electorate: group representation runs through the quotas of the proportional lists (Arts. 84(2) and 176), and voters abroad cannot vote.

classes.name: विशेष प्रयोजन निकाय
classes.name_en: Special-purpose bodies
classes.disposition_reason: The Constitution provides for special, protected, or autonomous areas (Art. 56(5)), but none has an elected body; cooperatives, bar associations, and user committees hold their own elections, which the Commission does not run.

classes.name: उम्मेदवार छनोट
classes.name_en: Party candidate selection
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose candidates and closed lists under their own statutes (Political Parties Act 2073); the state runs no primary and publishes no nomination vote.
